text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.14% today to $385.24, continuing a sharp five-day slide that has wiped out 7% of the stock's value since mid-September. The broader refining sector is caught in uncertainty over geopolitical risks: oil prices remain volatile amid unresolved tensions between Iran and the U.S., with Wall Street analysts openly admitting they don't know which way crude will move next. Adding pressure, refining margins are under strain as U.S. crude hovers near $96 per barrel while refineries run at 94% capacity—leaving less room for profitable operations if prices move the wrong way.

The uncertainty cuts both ways for a refiner like this one. While some headlines suggest potential diplomatic breakthroughs in the Middle East could lower oil prices and help margins, those same breakthroughs could reduce the supply-shock premium built into crude costs, hurting a company that benefits when oil is scarce and expensive. Until clarity emerges on Iran, Ukraine, or global supply, the stock remains caught between competing bullish and bearish scenarios.
